distribution.note: The repository is public and pre-release: no release tag exists and nothing is published to a package registry. Every install path is a checkout of this repository at a named commit, so a package-registry install command does not exist.

none.title: No test
none.meaning: No test in this repository exercises the engine through the adapter. An entry may still describe an interface, for example one that reports `unavailable`.
none.does_not_mean: That the engine or the adapter is broken; only that nothing has been shown.

offline-fake.title: Offline, against fakes
offline-fake.meaning: The adapter logic is tested against a fake driver or recorded engine output. The engine itself is not installed and nothing touches a browser or a device.
offline-fake.does_not_mean: That the engine works with the adapter; a fake only shows what the adapter does with what the fake returns.

engine-backed-ci.title: Real engine in a CI job
engine-backed-ci.meaning: A CI job installs the pinned engine (and the browser or server it needs) and runs the adapter against it; the job fails, never skips, when a dependency is missing or no test is collected.
engine-backed-ci.does_not_mean: Support for other engine versions, browsers, operating systems or architectures than the one named, or that a real device or emulator was driven.

device-backed-local.title: Real device or emulator, observed locally
device-backed-local.meaning: A real device or emulator was driven through the adapter by hand on a named machine and the run is recorded in the repository. No CI job repeats it.
device-backed-local.does_not_mean: That CI re-runs it, that it holds on another machine, API level or device, or that the run is reproducible by anyone without the same setup.

device-backed-ci.title: Real device or emulator in CI
device-backed-ci.meaning: A CI job drives a real device or emulator through the adapter and fails, never skips, when none is attached.
device-backed-ci.does_not_mean: Coverage beyond the device, operating system version and host named in the evidence.

appium_android: Android needs a compatible SDK, platform tools, a device or an emulator, the UiAutomator2 driver and host acceleration.
Starting the Appium server is not a successful real UI session: only an attached device or emulator driven through the adapter shows that.
The Android SDK, system images and emulator are the operator's, provisioned under Google's terms; they are never bundled or downloaded here.
appium_ios: iOS needs macOS, Xcode, WebDriverAgent and a supported simulator or device.
Linux containers are not a complete iOS solution.
The adapter reports UNAVAILABLE without a real, licensed worker; no iOS session has been run.
appium_general: A selected Appium adapter may generate client configuration while directing users to external device workers.
Never imply that a device or emulator is bundled with the runtime.

product_capabilities.title: One frozen plan run through two engines, Playwright Chromium and Robot Framework, with one evidence bundle (`redevops-qa run`, `redevops-qa demo`)
product_capabilities.summary: A plan is frozen (the strict runtime-contracts parser, every assertion's digest, the plan digest), the fixture app starts on loopback with a seeded defect or none, the browser lane and the Robot lane run one after the other as supervised child processes under one run id, and one evidence bundle is written. A seeded defect fails exactly its own lane and the other lane's result is still recorded.
product_capabilities.test_level_scope: the runner's end-to-end lane on a GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runner: real Chromium through Playwright 1.64.1 and Robot Framework 7.5 together, the fixture app only, each seeded defect, partial success, timeouts, cancellation and a killed parent checked with a process table

evidence.claim: real Chromium and Robot Framework 7.5 in one run, the two-lane plan for each seeded defect, timeouts, cancellation and a killed parent; the job fails on zero tests or any skip
the tests the end-to-end job runs

limitations: The target is the bundled fixture app: this release runs plans against it only, not against an arbitrary application.
Linux x86_64 only; Playwright with Chromium only; Selenium and Appium are not part of this workflow.

The browser lane's traffic goes through the egress gateway; a Robot lane that asks for the kernel layers (`origin-only`) is limited by them instead, with the limits the report states (against a hostile library only the port is enforced: a second thread can change a connect address to another one on the allowed port; files, pipes and processes are not confined), and does not start where they are unavailable; a Robot lane that says `not-enforced` is limited by nothing.
The pinned bundle's install and the public CI demo are run by CI jobs added after this evidence; they get their own rows once a run on the main branch backs them.

product_capabilities.title: Re-verification of a finished run from its evidence bundle alone (`redevops-qa verify`)
product_capabilities.summary: `verify` recomputes every digest, the frozen assertions and every verdict from the bundle in a process of its own and rejects any finding with exit status 5; `run` and `demo` end by calling it in a fresh interpreter. A tamper and negative suite is run over real bundles.
product_capabilities.test_level_scope: the end-to-end job (bundles of real engine runs, verified at the end of every run) and the offline runner job (the tamper and negative suite), on ubuntu-24.04

evidence.claim: every run in this job ends with `verify` in a separate process over the bundle the run wrote; the job installs Playwright 1.64.1 and Robot Framework 7.5
the offline runner suite, which includes the tamper and negative suite for `verify`
the tamper suite over real bundles

limitations: It is a re-verification by the same code the run used, in a separate process; it is not an independent implementation of the verdicts. `independent` here means independent of the engine's own status.

The hash chain inside a bundle is unkeyed: someone who can rewrite a whole bundle can rewrite its digests too. Only a manifest digest (the anchor) obtained from somewhere the producer cannot rewrite, passed with `--anchor`, shows that a bundle is the one the value was taken from; nothing in the tool authenticates where the value came from.
A verified run does not show that the application under test is correct.
